answer: In PoA, bonded escrows make each identity’s stake a real liability: when signed evidence links k identities to coordinated equivocation, pairwise attribution drives penalties to O(k²), not merely a per-node fee. A quill-marked commitment cannot hide shared control; detection applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery from restoring the original stake. Thus a sybil vine becomes increasingly costly to maintain, and one compromised kernel can expose the swarm to correlated slashing.
